result.title: Action-On-Item Preference Flow: A Shared Event Schema for Predictive and Generative Personalization
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Author-prepared archival version with expanded discussion and interpretation
result.summary: A user's movie, news, and dialogue histories differ in their native actions and outputs, yet each interaction supplies evidence that can update user memory. We study whether these histories can train one reusable update mechanism. An action-on-item schema pairs a mapped interaction role with a content embedding, allowing shared update parameters to operate on separate user states. We establish invariance to native relabeling, bounded state changes under item-embedding perturbations, and a pooled-training bound under explicit compatibility conditions. The Multi-Timescale State Hypothesis (MTSH) specifies how this evidence enters, persists, and is consumed; PerTIDE implements it with action gating, three state-space traces, fusion, and command-conditioned readout. On PENS, the same history encoder supports both next-news prediction and personalized headline generation. In a controlled PENS-to-MovieLens experiment, a frozen source-trained core exceeds an identically structured random core by 15.23 MRR points after fitting the same target consumer. On MIND, PerTIDE retains a 4.12-point MRR advantage over a same-input three-branch state-space control. Action, readout, and trace interventions identify complementary contributions to these gains. Together, the theory and experiments support learning history updates across compatible sources and reusing them through predictive and generative consumers.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「action-on-item」事件模式，用动作角色加内容嵌入构成统一历史更新机制，并以 PerTIDE（动作门控、三条状态空间轨迹、融合与指令条件读出）在新闻预测、个性化标题生成及跨域迁移上验证可复用更新参数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其动作门控、多时间尺度状态轨迹与命令条件读出的「证据如何进入、保持、被消费」框架，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态的多假设维护、证据筛选与何时读取 latent 内容的问题形成概念类比，可供核查。
